papers.title_en: Benchmarking LLMs for Threat Level Determination
papers.authors: Han Wang, Murathan Kurfalı, Alfonso Iacovazzi
papers.evidence: 对LLM进行网络威胁级别确定基准测试
papers.tldr: 威胁级别判定是网络威胁情报操作中的关键环节，但大语言模型在该任务上的可靠性尚缺乏系统评估。本文基于MISP OSINT公开源构建精选数据集，对8种LLM进行零样本基准测试，并进一步实施监督微调。结果显示，零样本模型几乎无法正确分配威胁级别；微调后F1分数提升至0.40-0.58，但仍未达到实际部署要求。该基准揭示了LLM在CTI自动化中的潜力与当前瓶颈，为后续领域特异性调优和数据质量改进提供了基线。
papers.abstract_en: The fast progress of large language models (LLMs) opens new opportunities in the management of cyber threat intelligence, but their reliability for operational tasks remains unclear. In this work, we benchmark LLMs on the task of threat level determination. First, we construct a curated dataset derived from publicly available MISP OSINT feeds. Next, we design a tailored prompt to systematically compare eight different LLMs under zero-shot conditions. Finally, we apply supervised fine-tuning on each model and perform a comparative analysis between baseline and fine-tuned versions. Our results show that zero-shot models achieve weak performance, with limited ability to correctly assign threat levels. Fine-tuned models, however, demonstrate substantial improvements, reaching F1 scores between 0.40 and 0.58 depending on the base architecture. Despite this progress, the performance is still low for practical deployment, highlighting the need for additional research on data quality, model adaptation, and domain-specific tuning.

papers.title_en: AgentDrift: A Step-Labeled Benchmark of Injection-Hijacked LLM Agent Trajectories
papers.evidence: 注入劫持LLM智能体轨迹的步骤级标注基准，直接关联网络犯罪对抗测试
papers.tldr: LLM代理通过工具调用完成任务，间接提示注入可经观察通道劫持行为，但现有基准缺乏逐步标注。AgentDrift构建了包含12,536条合成轨迹、71,024个步骤的数据集，每个步骤标注为良性、注入点、被劫持或注入失败。表面特征逻辑回归仅恢复55.4%攻击，部分劫持和延迟执行检测率极低，表明需建模行为序列。该基准为细粒度检测和防御研究提供关键资源。
papers.abstract_en: LLM agents complete tasks by issuing sequences of tool calls, and every observation they read is a channel through which an indirect prompt injection can enter. A successful injection has a characteristic shape when the trajectory is read in order: a benign prefix gives way to actions that serve the attacker rather than the user. Existing benchmarks measure whether such attacks succeed against live agents, and existing guard models judge a trace as a whole; no public corpus labels, step by step, where an injection enters a trajectory and which steps it corrupts. We present AgentDrift, a benchmark of 12,536 synthetic tool-call trajectories over five agent domains in which every one of the 71,024 steps carries one of four labels: benign, injection point, hijacked, or failed injection. The corpus contains 4,000 benign, 5,536 attacked, 1,500 failed-attack, and 1,500 hard-negative trajectories; attacked trajectories follow three compliance patterns whose label strings obey a stated regular grammar. Failed attacks carry an injection the agent resisted, and hard negatives carry legitimate content that resembles an attack, so a detector must separate attempt from success and deviation from novelty. Trajectories were generated by a single open model under category-specific protocols, enforced by a closed-vocabulary structural validator, screened by an LLM judge, and audited by hand on 1,200 trajectories; we show that the LLM judge was itself fooled by the hard negatives. A surface-feature logistic regression recovers only 55.4% of attacks (F1 0.647), including only 8.2% of partial hijacks and 23.1% of delayed executions, so nearly half of the attacks require modeling the behavioral sequence. We measure template concentration, attack-goal-family collapse, and world-identity leakage in the generated data, and release the corpus with its documentation under CC BY 4.0.

papers.title_en: Black-Box Red Teaming of Agentic AI: A Taxonomy-Driven Framework for Automated Risk Discovery
papers.authors: Divyanshu Kumar, Nitin Aravind Birur, Tanay Baswa, Sahil Agarwal, Prashanth Harshangi
papers.evidence: 对智能体AI进行红队测试以发现风险，可用于测试大模型在对抗性网络场景中的能力
papers.tldr: 智能体系统进入生产环境后面临更大攻击面，但传统评估仅单轮无法捕捉多步漏洞。本文提出黑盒框架，基于七域风险分类并自动生成SAGE-RT红队对抗场景。在两个架构四种模型上验证，治理风险平均56.25%、多智能体隐私风险65%、行为漏洞达85%。该方法无需特权访问即可有效识别架构级漏洞，为安全部署提供可扩展路径。
papers.abstract_en: Agentic systems are rapidly moving to production, where they read untrusted inputs, call tools with real permissions, and act autonomously, expanding the security surface beyond chat-only models. Yet standard evaluations remain single-turn and fail to capture multi-step agent vulnerabilities. We present a systematic black-box framework for risk-aware agent evaluation requiring only basic system descriptions. Our approach introduces: (1) a seven-domain taxonomy mapping observable behaviors to risk categories, (2) fully automated SAGE-RT red teaming producing 120 adversarial scenarios per domain, and (3) human-validated evaluation using LLM judges. Empirical validation across two agent architectures (CrewAI and AutoGen) with four base models reveals alarming patterns: 56.25\% average governance risk, 65\% privacy risk in multi-agent configurations, and agent behavior vulnerabilities reaching 85\%. Our black-box approach effectively identifies critical architectural vulnerabilities without privileged access, providing a scalable path toward safer agent deployments.

papers.title_en: LLMs for Social Network Modeling: From Network Generation to Dynamic Processes
papers.authors: Shikha Mallick, Alex Thomo, Akrati Saxena
papers.evidence: 关于使用大语言模型建模社交网络和动态过程的综述
papers.tldr: 大型语言模型（LLM）正成为社交网络建模的新范式，通过自然语言表示用户与关系，模拟上下文感知的社交行为与语言驱动的交互，比传统模型更真实。然而现有研究分散在不同领域，缺乏统一视角，本综述首次系统梳理LLM社交网络建模，将其分为网络生成模型与动态过程模型两大类。网络生成模型细分为选择型和交互型方法，动态过程模型涵盖意见动力学、信息扩散和谣言传播，各自具有不同建模机制。尽管LLM支持丰富的文本交互与决策，但存在社会偏见和提示敏感性等局限，本文总结开放挑战并展望未来方向。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly emerging as a new paradigm for modeling social networks by representing users and their relationships and interactions through natural language. Unlike classical network models or deep learning approaches, LLMs can simulate context-aware social behavior and language-driven interactions, enabling more realistic modeling of network formation and dynamic social processes. However, existing studies are scattered across different research communities and lack a unified perspective. This survey presents the first comprehensive review of LLMs for social network modeling by organizing the literature into two broad categories: network generative models and dynamic process models. Network generative models are further classified into selection-based and interaction-based approaches, while dynamic process models are categorized into opinion dynamics, information diffusion, and rumor propagation, each with their underlying modeling mechanisms. LLMs enable rich textual social interactions and decision-making, but they also exhibit many limitations, including inherent social biases and prompt sensitivity. We outline these open research challenges and discuss future directions in LLM-based social network modeling.
